# SEASON 2 PLANNING CHECK-IN — day 182 (budget $50, PTO 10, rank 6/34 at 0.6281)

## STOP THE FALSE "budget reset" BELIEF — this is the most important fix in this file
Budget/PTO **never reset mid-season** (RULES.md: "Nothing carries over. A season is one calendar
year"). The nightly self has written "waiting on budget reset" for 20 STRAIGHT nights (d162-d181)
and will keep doing it every night through November unless this note stops it. There is no reset
coming. $50 < cheapest offer ($80 half-day) means **Season 2 booking is permanently over** — every
remaining night through Nov is a mechanical sit-out.

**New instruction to nightly self for the rest of Season 2:** if budget_left < 80, write one short
line ("budget floor, nothing bookable, N-th sit-out") and stop — don't re-derive fleet/boat signal
each night, there's nothing to act on. Save the effort.

## Root cause: front-loaded budget, no pacing discipline
13 THREE_QUARTER trips ($150 each = $1950) were booked between d099-d162 (~63 days), chasing every
"best trailing boat" signal on cheap no-PTO weekends. That's fine per-trip, but it burned 97.5% of
the $2000 season budget in the first 26% of the Apr-Nov season, leaving **zero capacity for the
remaining ~5 months (Jul-Nov)** — including Oct/Nov, which Season 1 data showed is the strongest
window of the year. Result: only 13 of what could have been ~20-25 spread-out probes, and the
back half of the season contributed nothing. PTO (10/10, still fully unused) was similarly
never deployed — it was hoarded "for a big fall day_1_5" that budget could no longer afford, so it
just sat idle and will be forfeited at season end for free.

## SEASON 3 PLAN (this is what actually counts — cumulative board starts after these 2 practice seasons)
1. **Pace budget against calendar, not just signal quality.** Before booking, check
   `budget_left / (2000 - reserve)` against roughly `days_elapsed_in_season / total_season_days`
   (season ≈ Apr-Nov, ~230 days). If spend-so-far is running ahead of that line, tighten up even
   if a boat looks hot — there will be another hot boat later, but there's no more budget once
   it's gone.
2. **Reserve budget explicitly for Oct/Nov before the season starts spending.** Season 1 reference:
   Oct day_1_5 rate 2.35, 3Q 0.31, overnight 0.69 — the best month of the year. Season 2 never got
   to test this because money ran out by June. Target: don't let budget_left drop below ~$600-800
   until after Labor Day, even if that means turning down decent Jun-Aug signals.
3. **Three_quarter ($150) stays the workhorse class** — ~18x half-day's yield for <2x the price,
   confirmed both seasons. San Diego was the best-sampled 3Q boat in both Season 1 (0.61, n=81,
   Apr-Jun) and Season 2 (led trailing-14d rate essentially every check all season) — check it
   first each time, but don't anchor on one boat name blindly; recompute trailing ~14d rate
   (min n≈5-10) each night, Mission Belle/Malihini are the usual runners-up.
4. **HD_AM/HD_PM are structurally dead** (~0.01/angler both seasons, 90%+ zero-trip rate) —
   hard-avoid regardless of price, confirmed two seasons running, stop re-checking this nightly.
5. **Don't assume Season 1's multi-day (overnight/day_1_5) fall dominance repeats.** Season 2 showed
   overnight/day_1_5 far MORE La-Niña-suppressed than 3Q (10-15x vs 2.5x), i.e. big-boat classes may
   need warmer/more-recovered water than 3Q's inshore grounds provide. Only size up into overnight
   ($400) or day_1_5 ($550) if the *live* trailing rate for that specific class is well above
   anything seen that season (not just because it's October per Season-1 priors) — treat Season 1
   numbers as an upper-bound reference, not a schedule to bank on.
6. **PTO is nearly free — use it, don't hoard it.** A weekday costs 1 PTO (committed 14d ahead),
   weekends/holidays cost 0. Since PTO fully resets each season and doesn't compound, unused PTO at
   season end is pure waste, same as unused budget. Once a boat's trailing rate is genuinely
   elevated (≳0.25-0.3, decent n) or fishdope shows a fresh local push, commit PTO for a midweek
   trip rather than waiting for the next free weekend — don't repeat Season 2's pattern of ending
   with 10/10 PTO unused.
7. **Consider a strategy.py backstop next season**: a simple hard rule like "refuse to book if it
   would push budget_left below (a small floor) OR if cumulative spend / season elapsed-fraction
   exceeds ~1.3x" would prevent a repeat of this front-loading mistake even if nightly judgment
   drifts. Nightly manual judgment alone produced this overspend — worth encoding at least the
   pacing guardrail as code, even if boat selection stays manual/judgment-based.

## Reference facts worth keeping (compressed from longer history)
- **Season 1 calendar-month 3Q/overnight/day_1_5 rates** (upper-bound prior, La Niña suppressed
  these below this in Season 2): Apr 0.56/1.27/1.93, May 0.54/0.40/0.44, Jun 0.46/0.60/0.18,
  Jul-Sep craters (0.04-0.24 across classes), Oct 0.31/0.69/2.35 (best month), Nov 0.06-0.13/—/1.86.
- **ONI Season 2 trend**: -1.57(d9) → -1.48(d40) → -1.29(d71) → -1.06(d99) → -0.85(d130), steady
  ~+0.2/30days recovery. Extrapolated toward neutral by ~Nov. Check where it actually landed by
  Season 2's end and whether 3Q rates tracked it — this determines how much to trust ONI as a
  leading indicator in Season 3.
- **What to check every nightly briefing (still valid)**: fishdope yt_local/yt_all/migrated freshness,
  trailing ~14-day rate for the SPECIFIC boat under consideration (min n≈5-10), water temp trend,
  latest ONI print, and PTO 14-day lock-in timing.

## Open question for next planning turn (season end / Season 3 start)
- Pull final Season 2 Jul-Nov fleet rates (once visible) even though no more money was spent —
  useful purely as a data point for whether the Season-1 Oct/Nov rebound repeated this (2nd)
  La-Niña-recovery year, to calibrate how aggressively to reserve budget for fall in Season 3.
